data: Tools and Methods in Environmental Studies

This course will provide the basic vocabulary that students require to navigate the environmental sciences, humanities, and social sciences. Through systematic close readings of influential texts, we hope to enable students to use the tools and methods employed by these disciplines in the context of the environmental studies. We begin the course by charting out primary motivators and drivers of work in each discipline. We will then home in on cutting-edge research within each discipline. For example, in the environmental sciences, we will focus on the concept of thresholds and safe operating spaces for humanity. During our engagement with the environmental humanities, we will focus on how progress in the digital humanities has enabled visualisation and textual analysis of environmental history, philosophy, ethics, literary theory, art, and education. Lastly, in the environmental social sciences, we will pinpoint how ethnography and narratives are now becoming invaluable tools for understanding how society interacts with the environment.
Sundaram Fasteners Associate Professor, Environmental Studies
